0.long_answer: Carpenter syndrome is an autosomal recessive disorder that is caused by mutations in the RAB23 gene. This syndrome is clinically characterized by craniosynostosis, polysyndactyly, and other anomalies, including brachydactyly. Brachydactyly refers to the presence of abnormally short fingers or toes, which is one of the features observed in Carpenter syndrome. The connection between RAB23 mutations and the clinical manifestations of Carpenter syndrome, including brachydactyly, has been elucidated in various studies, establishing a clear link between the gene defect and the phenotypic manifestations of the syndrome.
